Released: 15 October 2026

## Highlights

- The operator now hands the write and Raft leaderships of a PGD node off before its pod is evicted, for example by `kubectl drain`. The eviction is rejected with `429 Too Many Requests`, which the drain retries, while another pod of the PGD group is unavailable or the hand-off runs. The hand-off is bounded by the Raft election timeouts of the node, 160 seconds with the defaults; one that can't finish in that time admits the eviction with a warning. See [Eviction held, drain retrying](../trouble_shooting/#eviction-held-drain-retrying).
- The operator deployment now runs two replicas, with a `PodDisruptionBudget` of `maxUnavailable: 1` and a soft pod anti-affinity that spreads them over different nodes, so a webhook endpoint stays up while a node drains. Every replica serves the webhooks; the controllers run on the leader.

## Upgrade notes

- The `PodDisruptionBudget` of a PGD group now selects the pods of the group by the `k8s.enterprisedb.io/podRole: instance` label, which a pod has from its creation, instead of the `k8s.enterprisedb.io/instanceRole` label, which CNP sets once the instance runs. A recreated pod is now covered by the budget until it's Ready. The operator patches the budget of existing groups after the upgrade.
- The webhook server accepts any client on port 9443, and the pod eviction webhook has side effects: any workload that reaches that port on the operator pods can send forged eviction reviews. Restrict ingress to that port with a `NetworkPolicy`, see [Webhooks](../security/#webhooks).

## Supported versions

- Kubernetes: 1.34, 1.35, 1.36, and 1.37
- PostgreSQL: 18, 17, 16, 15, and 14
- The tested PG4K version is v1.28.5

This release of EDB Postgres® AI for CloudNativePG™ Global Cluster includes the following:

## Features

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>The common name of the node server certificates can now use a different domain than the one the nodes connect to, by setting <code>spec.connectivity.tls.serverCert.commonNameDomain</code>. This helps when a certificate authority requires a specific domain in the common name. See <a href="../certificates/#common-name-domain">Common name domain</a>.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
